assignment: Advise a committee choosing between two sites under a two-criterion index.
source: On a 0–100 scale, site A scores 80 for access and 50 for cost performance. Site B scores 60 and 80 respectively. The index weights access by w and cost by 1−w. A committee favors w=0.7 but another group favors w=0.4. Scores carry several points of measurement uncertainty.

criteria.full: Derives A = 50+30w, B = 80−20w and the tie at w=0.6.
criteria.partial: Finds the correct winner at one weight without locating the switch.

criteria.full: Computes A/B as 71/66 at 0.7 and 62/72 at 0.4 or equivalent checked differences.
Explains how score uncertainty near the boundary can change a decision and suggests sensitivity ranges.
criteria.partial: Treats the weights as the sole source of uncertainty.

criteria.full: Asks stakeholders to justify weights before selection and records tradeoffs or robustness conditions.
criteria.partial: Chooses weights after seeing the preferred winner without disclosure.
